column7: 2026-11-03: parseBytes supports only plain numbers/B and binary units (KiB..YiB); kB/MB/GB etc. deliberately throw until user confirms with storage team how to read them

2026-11-03: Storage team decision: users paste from Windows Explorer, so on this branch non-i units (KB or kB, MB, GB...) are powers of 1024 (1 KB = 1024, 1 MB = 1048576). To be added in a later change; parseBytes still throws for them.

2026-11-03: billing-svc decision: when decimal units (kB, MB, GB...) are added to parseBytes on this branch, they are strict SI powers of 1000 (1 MB = 1,000,000 bytes), matching prettyBytes output. This intentionally differs from storage-app, which reads KB/MB/GB as 1024. Until then they still throw.
2026-11-03: parseBytes now accepts kB/KB, MB..YB as powers of 1024 (per storage-team decision); only case variants like kb/mB and bit units throw
